name: Do I need a permit for a small bump-out addition in Los Angeles or the Valley?

mainEntity.name: At what size does a bump-out or small room addition stop being exempt and require a permit in Los Angeles-area cities?
mainEntity.text: At what size does a bump-out or small room addition stop being exempt and require a permit in Los Angeles-area cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small bump-out can still require a permit if it changes the home’s footprint, exterior wall line, foundation, roof structure, or any mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems. In Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and nearby communities, the key question is whether the work is structural or affects code compliance, not whether it looks minor. Even modest additions may need architectural plans, structural calculations, energy forms, and separate permits for plumbing, electrical, and HVAC work. Before designing, verify zoning setbacks, lot coverage, and any hillside, fire, or historic restrictions that may apply. A good rule of thumb is that if walls are being moved, new square footage is being added, or the roofline changes, a permit is likely required. The safest next step is a pre-submittal check with the local building department using a site plan and rough scope of work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most bump-outs that change the home’s footprint, exterior walls, or structural framing require a permit, even if the added area is small. In Los Angeles-area jurisdictions, the trigger is usually the type of work, not just the square footage. If the project alters structure, utilities, setbacks, or lot coverage, expect plan check and permits.
